scene.note: The same few lines are written once and wrapped around any handler, which goes on working as before.

steps.note: The desk calls a wrapped handler with its usual values.
The wrapper says which handler is running.
The handler gets exactly the values the desk gave, and its answer goes back unchanged.
A wrapped handler starts the night with a count of 0.
Each call adds one to that handler's own count, and the handler works as before.
Dougie reads how many times each handler ran, one count per handler.
A wrapped handler is given a clock to read, the computer's own unless another is handed in.
Each call reads the clock before and after, and notes the seconds it took.
Dougie reads every call's time, under the handler's own name.
Paging a team is a handler like any other.
One line above it puts the counting wrapper on it.
Every page sent is now counted, and pages go out as before.
